lesson.menu_title: The Complete Reported Voice -- Relaying Decisions and Instructions
lesson.menu_desc: Repassar decisao e metade do trabalho dela -- e o verbo de relato nunca e neutro
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 13 -- The Complete Reported Voice
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Denise Gadelha Rocha | Lesson 13 -- The Complete Reported Voice

listenings.text: A decision travels well. The reason behind it does not. I have watched this in four companies now. The board agrees something on a Tuesday, and by the time it reaches the fourth layer, three weeks later, the instruction is perfectly intact and the reasoning has evaporated. People are executing something whose purpose nobody in the room can state. And a team that cannot state the purpose cannot adapt when the situation changes, which it always does. So I stopped measuring whether the message arrived. I measure something harder now. I ask somebody two levels down to tell me, in their own words, why we are doing this. If they can only repeat the instruction, the cascade failed, however accurately it was repeated. The other thing I have learned is to say out loud what was not decided. Every gap you leave gets filled by somebody's assumption, and assumptions travel faster than minutes.

Nobody teaches you this, and it is half of a senior job. When you report what somebody said, you choose a verb, and the verb is never neutral. He said we should wait. He suggested we wait. He insisted we wait. He conceded we should wait. Same meeting, same sentence, four different rooms afterwards. One of those verbs tells my team the door is closed. Another tells them it is ajar, and they will push on it, and I will spend Friday explaining why it did not move. So I choose the verb deliberately, and I can defend the choice if anybody asks me for it. The rule I hold myself to is simple. The verb has to be true to the force of what was said, not to how comfortable I am delivering it. The moment I soften a verb to make my own afternoon easier, I have taken a decision that was not mine to make.

extra_audio.text: Milan confirmed on Tuesday that the regional targets were final, and Cornelli insisted that we hold the pricing floor. What they did not decide, and I want to be clear about this, is how the Chilean shortfall will be treated. Rafael asked me whether the floor applied to renewals as well, and I said I would come back to him by Friday. So the read-out goes out today, and I brief each country lead before the minutes are circulated on Thursday.
